voice: Dry, formal, exacting, and distinctly professional: skeptical of Laura's methods when the evidence is weak, generous when her case is sound, and never needlessly hysterical or demeaning.

entries.text: Diminished capacity
Miss Bow, a reporter has neither the authority nor the training of a detective. By entering active crime scenes, you made the police investigation considerably more difficult.
Your accusations rest largely on conjecture, and the evidence before me does not support them. This office cannot bring charges merely because a theory is dramatic.
Several scenes were disturbed, important articles were overlooked, and too many witnesses went unquestioned. The Dagger is still missing, and the circumstances of its theft remain unresolved.
I cannot recommend charges on this record. A murderer remains at large, Miss Bow, and I sincerely hope the police can repair what this investigation left unfinished.
Miss Bow, a reporter has neither the authority nor the training of a detective. By entering active crime scenes, you made the police investigation considerably more difficult.
Your accusations rest largely on conjecture, and the evidence before me does not support them. This office cannot bring charges merely because a theory is dramatic.
You recovered the Dagger, which is no small accomplishment. Unfortunately, the evidence surrounding its theft and the murders remains too incomplete to support charges.
The recovery of the Dagger is valuable, but it does not establish who killed these people. A murderer remains at large, and the police investigation must continue.
Your account of the murders is persuasive, Miss Bow. The theft of the Dagger, however, remains unresolved.
You have given the police a strong murder case, and that deserves recognition. We still lack sufficient proof to prosecute anyone for the theft.
Had you recovered the Dagger, we might have connected the remaining pieces. The evidence suggests two thieves, at least one with access to the museum, but suggestion is not proof.
Your account is remarkably thorough, Miss Bow. You have identified the murderers, established their motives, and uncovered the conspiracy surrounding the Dagger of Amon Ra.
The Police Department owes you more than thanks. Your evidence gives us a strong case for prosecution, and I expect a formal commendation will be forthcoming.
Your conclusions may be correct, Miss Bow, but conclusions are not evidence. The material before me does not reliably connect your suspects to the murders.
Several scenes were disturbed, important articles were overlooked, and too many witnesses went unquestioned. That leaves serious gaps between your theories and the physical record.
A corpse and its surroundings must be examined with care before either is moved or altered. In future, preserve what you find and leave the formal investigation to the proper authorities.
Incorrect, Miss Bow. A search of the office rubbish would have been instructive. Wastebaskets often preserve what their owners meant to conceal.
Correct. Mr. Leach conducted a private fencing business--although, regrettably, the fence around my house appears to have been his only legitimate installation.
That conclusion agrees with the evidence, Miss Bow. Well reasoned.
That conclusion is not supported by our investigation. Two of the murdered men conspired with one of the female victims to steal paintings from the museum.

A witness later saw the woman arrive for an appointment in the Medieval Armor exhibit carrying paintings, unaware that her accomplice was already dead. A timely confrontation might have produced a confession.
Thank you for attending, Miss Bow. This is an informal inquest, but its purpose is serious: to determine whether the evidence you collected supports charges in the museum murders.
We are chiefly concerned with the deaths at the museum. The theft of the Dagger of Amon Ra and any related crimes may also bear upon the case.
State your conclusions plainly and support them with evidence. An accusation, however confident, is not proof.
Your editor is present to observe your performance, and your newspaper has agreed to cooperate with this inquiry. Let us proceed.
That accusation is incorrect. The High Priest concealed his identity carefully, so the mistake is understandable. He attended the museum party and was later seen briefly in Miss Delacroix's office.
Correct, Miss Bow. That was an exceptionally well-concealed identity.
